Arthur adjusted his tie, sweating through his shirt as he stared at the parrot perched on the conference table. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Arthur had made a catastrophic error in judgment. He had brought Barnaby, his African Grey, to the office. He had not anticipated that Barnaby had been listening to Arthur’s late-night calls with the CEO.

"Good morning, everyone," Arthur said, his voice cracking. "I’d like to introduce you to Barnaby. He’s... very social."

Barnaby tilted his head, looked directly at the VP of Sales, and squawked, "The Q3 projections are fake! We’re bankrupt! Also, tell me what tool you use to clean your teeth."

The room went silent. The VP of Sales dropped his coffee mug.

Arthur lunged for the birdcage. "He’s joking! It’s a bit! A dark, corporate satire!"

Barnaby flapped his wings and shouted, "The CEO is embezzling funds! And I need a floss pick! A floss pick, Arthur!"

"Shut up, Barnaby!" Arthur hissed, trying to cover the bird’s beak with his hand.

Barnaby bit Arthur’s thumb. "Ouch! He’s biting me! The CEO is embezzling funds! And I need a floss pick!"

The HR director stood up, pale. "Arthur, did your parrot just confess to financial fraud?"

"No!" Arthur yelled, wrestling the bird. "He’s mimicking! He’s a mimic! Like a tape recorder! A very loud, very specific tape recorder!"

Barnaby broke free, flew to the top of the whiteboard, and screamed, "THE SECRET SAUCE RECIPE IS IN THE CEO’S DESK DRAWER! AND I NEED A FLOSS PICK!"

Arthur grabbed a stack of confidential files and threw them at the bird. "Stop it! Stop talking about the secret sauce!"

Barnaby caught a file in his talons, looked at the VP, and said, "This file is empty. Just like our profits. And I need a floss pick."

The CEO walked in, holding a donut. "What’s all the noise about? Why is everyone staring at the bird?"
